title: Ross Jenkins on Starting Your Marketing: A Checklist of Basic Channels
summary: A generic beginner checklist for small-business marketing: plan first, build a website, show up on social media, claim your online listings, run a few targeted ads, network locally, use coupons and free trials, and stay consistent. Broad and light on specifics, but a usable starting list.

principles.text: Great products aren't enough; strong marketing sets you apart and can carry even mediocre products.
principles.quote: it is not enough to simply have high-quality products and services. You also need to have a strong marketing game so that you can set yourself apart from your competitors

principles.text: Start with a simple plan tied to ROI, plus a 30-second pitch tested on people in advance.
principles.quote: You do not have to make your plan big. What is important is that it is beneficial for your ROI.

principles.text: Control what people find when they search for you by claiming your business listings.
principles.quote: You would want to see and control what people read about your products or services when they search for you.

principles.text: In paid search, pick a few quality keywords rather than many, and use location and budget controls.
principles.quote: Rather than picking out a lot of keywords, it is best to choose a few quality keywords.

principles.text: Free trials and coupons start building followers, since satisfied customers return and share their experience.
principles.quote: A customer who is satisfied with what you have to offer will return and share his or her experience with his or her family and friends.

principles.text: Be consistent; people can't buy from a business they don't know exists.
principles.quote: you have to be consistent. You have to make sure that your business is known.
